4001.t: Uncertain. Seems to go back to a stem *φραδ-.

4015.t: Traditionally considered related to ψάω (psáō, “to rub smooth, crumble”), though the morphological function of -φ- (-ph-) would be unclear.

4056.t: Pre-Greek origin, although related to Latin arānea. Whether it is the source of the Latin term or they both originated from a different common source is unclear.

4026.t: From ἀ- (a-, privative alpha) + μιαίνω (miaínō, “stain, defile”) + -τος (-tos).

4070.t: From Proto-Hellenic *árotron, from Proto-Indo-European *h₂érh₃trom, from *h₂erh₃- + *-trom; equivalent to ἀρόω (aróō, “to plough”) + -τρον (-tron, instrument noun suffix).

4007.t: From χείμερος (kheímeros, “wintry, stormy”) + -ινός (-inós), or directly from Proto-Indo-European [Term?] and cognate with Latin hībernus.

4071.t: Zero grade of μέχρι (mékhrĭ), from Proto-Indo-European *méǵʰ(s)ri. The genitive is from the PIE ablative of comparison/extent.

4018.t: From ἀγρεύς (ăgreús, “hunter”) + -εύω (-eúō, verb-forming suffix), from ἄγρα (ắgrā, “hunt”); doublet of ἀγρέω (ăgréō).

4089.t: From Proto-Hellenic *eləpʰrós, from Proto-Indo-European *h₁ln̥gʷʰrós (“lightweight”). See also ἐλαχύς (elăkhŭ́s, “small, short”).

4074.t: From ἀνδρο- (ăndro-, “man”) + νίκη (nī́kē, “victory”) + -ος (-os). Compare Νίκανδρος (Nī́kăndros), which contains the first two components in the opposite order.

4083.t: From ἐκ- (ek-, “out of”) + πλήσσω (plḗssō, “to strike, to smite”).

4021.t: From ἀκριβής (akrībḗs) + -ια (-ia). Synchronically analyzable as ἀκριβής (akrībḗs) + -εια (-eia).

4087.t: From ἐλαττόω (elattóō), Attic variant of ἐλασσόω (elassóō, “to make smaller, lessen”), + -σις (-sis).

4076.t: From ἐγ- (eg-) + καινός (kainós) + -ια (-ia). Semantic loan from Biblical Hebrew חֲנֻכָּה (ḥănukkâ).

4000.t: From the verb φρίσσω (phríssō, “to shiver, shudder, tremble”).

4062.t: ἀ- (a-) + φθαρσία (phtharsía), equivalent to ἄφθαρτος (áphthartos, “indestructible, immortal, eternal”) + -ία (-íā).
